messages:
mohit: FYI I hit a reproducible crash in the onboarding sample app when the API returns a validation error as text/plain. stack: AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get' in error handling path
elaine: ugh. sync or async client?
mohit: sync client (redwood.Client). async client seems to parse the body and give a dict. sync path leaves body as raw string, then our error handler does `.body.get(...)` and boom.
ana: do you have a minimal repro? can paste code + response?
mohit: minimal repro below. this is from the sample-app quickstart:```python
client = redwood.Client(api_key=env.API_KEY)
res = client.generate(model="open-01", input="trigger validation")
# server responds 422 with Content-Type: text/plain and body: "invalid input: missing field foo"
```
traceback:```
File ".../redwood/sdk/errors.py", line 42, in _raise_api_error
  details = exc.body.get("errors", [])
AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'
```
jon: this explains a bunch — we've had several bug reports where handlers assume parsed json. sometimes upstream returns plain text (nginx/ingress errors, or legacy infra). our async client pipeline runs `safe_json = try_parse_json(resp.text)` earlier and attaches `resp.json_body` so exception code uses that. sync client apparently doesn't for perf reasons.
elaine: thanks for the repro. short term we should stop calling `.get` on body without guard. long term we need a consistent exception shape across sync/async: BaseAPIError.body: Optional[dict], BaseAPIError.raw_text: str, and helper `body_as_dict()` to coerce. also update type stubs so mypy knows `.body` can be None.
mohit: agreed. adding a test reproducing text/plain 422 in both clients would catch regressions.
ana: quick patch idea: in errors._raise_api_error do:
```py
if isinstance(exc.body, str):
    exc.raw_text = exc.body
    exc.body = None
# safe access: if exc.body: details = exc.body.get("errors") else: details = []
```
jon: also add `__all__` export and docstring on the error class so dx sample apps can import typed exceptions and `except redwood.errors.BaseAPIError as e:` still works with typing.
elaine: small nit: we should keep a `parsed_json` attribute instead of overloading `body` — avoids changing public `body` semantics mid-release. but semver note: this is a fix not a breaking change if we keep compat.
mohit: I'll open a PR with tests and a sample-app tweak. linking issue in case it matters: #2543 (validation-body-parity)
devx-bot: Created issue #2543: "validation-body-parity across sync/async clients" by @mohit :eyes:
jon: ping @elaine for review when PR is up. probably a patch release to 0.18.x. we should add a changelog entry: "Fix: robust parsing of non-JSON error bodies in Python SDK (sync/async parity)"
elaine: will review. also let's add a mypy unit to CI that imports exception types from package-level modules to catch export regressions.
mohit: thanks all — leaving the repro branch in the sample-app under `repro/422-text` so docs team can reference it for onboarding notes.
ana: nice. after fix we should add a short note in onboarding FAQ: "what to do if your upstream returns non-JSON error responses" with the sample snippet. :white_check_mark:
